detail: When a native gate exceeds its timeout, gate.py SIGTERMs the process group and closes the pipe while the output-streaming thread is still blocked in read(), which raises ValueError: I/O operation on closed file. Because that happens last, it becomes the final thing in the job log, so a gate that timed out is presented as a crash inside the harness. macos-swiftui failed exactly this way: the appium smoke was Terminated at its timeout and the real cause sat two hundred lines above a Python traceback pointing at gate.py. The verdict was never wrong, since execute() already returned timed-out and the gate still failed, so this is an attribution defect rather than a correctness one. Attribution is the product's whole business: a criu restore hang that read as a product regression cost a full investigation the same day, and a harness that blames itself for a child's timeout is that mistake pointed inward. The read now returns on a closed stream instead of raising. HONEST LIMIT: the CI race did not reproduce on this machine, where a timed-out child returns timed-out with and without the guard, so the local check proves the timeout path still reports correctly and NOT that it reproduces the traceback. The guard is correct by construction, a closed pipe having nothing left to stream, rather than proven against the failure it was written for.
